assets.subjectEn: Exactly THREE DIFFERENT TYPE-A STEPPED PUNCH DESIGNS in one coherent product-series photograph. The point is different construction styles, not the same design scaled to different lengths or diameters. The required distinct pieces are: LEFT: a conventional single-step round punch. One slim cylindrical cutting section above one larger support shank, with a distinct square annular shoulder and only a tiny root radius. A modest round retaining foot at the bottom. Two body diameters above the foot. No intermediate cylinder. CENTER: a visibly different heavy multi-stage stepped punch, with THREE stacked cylindrical body tiers above a modest retaining foot: a broad lower support barrel, a medium-diameter middle stage, and a slim upper working cylinder. Two widely separated square annular shoulders. The broad barrel is prominent, making a strong architectural staircase silhouette. Not a scaled copy of the left punch. RIGHT: a slender fine-tip punch whose support body transitions through a clearly visible LONG CONICAL SHOULDER to the very thin straight cylindrical working needle. The conical neck is the defining feature, distinct from the square shoulders on the other two. A small retaining foot at the bottom. Flat working end, never a sharp pointed needle. Stand the three separately on their retaining feet in a lightly staggered group, working ends upward, with the bulky multi-tier design in the center. Use a mildly elevated three-quarter view so shoulders and flat working faces are visible. Every complete silhouette must be readable without overlap. Shared neutral silver-gray ground-metal finish and the approved light-gray studio background. These are structural catalog examples, no standard numbers, labels or dimensions. No three copies, no same topology at different scales, no decorative grooves, no extra flanges or fourth object.
